Here we discuss our individual patient problems through series of inputs from available global online community of experts with an aim to solve those patient's clinical problems with collective current best evidence based inputs.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThis e-log book also reflects my patient centered online learning portfolio and your valuable comments in comment box are most welcomed.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EI have been given this case to solve in an attempt to understand the topic of \"Patient clinical data analysis\" to develop my competency in reading and comprehending clinical data including history, clinical findings, investigations and to come up with a diagnosis and treatment plan.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA 50 years old male, tiles repair worker by occupation and resident of Bhongir , presented with \u003Cu\u003Echief complaints\u003C\/u\u003E of fever since 2 months, loss of appetite since 2 months, pain in abdomen 20 days back and yellowish discoloration of eyes since 20 days.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003EHistory of presenting illness\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient was apparently asymptomatic 2 months back , then he developed fever which was insidious in onset, intermittent in nature, low grade with no rigors and chills, no aggrevating and relieving factors.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENow, since 20 days, his fever usually spikes at evening which would continue the whole night, and reduce by morning, and is associated with chills.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFever was not associated with nausea, vomitings, headache and constipation.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHe also lost his appetite gradually since 2 months, which increased more 20 days back, with history of weight loss since 20 days.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient had decreased appetite since 2 months associated with nausea while eating, which resolved over time.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHis appetite decreased further and he didn't eat rice since 3 days, and now since 2 days his appetite increased a little again.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient also complained of pain in abdomen in the umbilical and right lumbar region, which was insidious in onset, gradually progressive, non radiating, aggravated while walking (around 100 metres)\u0026nbsp; and relieved on rest.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENow he doesn't have any pain.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHe had sensation of burning while micturition, not a\/w urgency, frequency, incontinence, polyuria, polydipsia, nocturia, urethral discharge.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThen later he had decreased appetite, weight loss and fever for which he came to kamineni.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo history of itching.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo history of flatulence, bloating\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo H\/o pedal edema, SOB, chest palpitations, chest pain and tightness.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient was diagnosed HIV positive 3 days back.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003EPast History\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient is known case of pulmonary tuberculosis 25 years ago, for which he used medication for 6 months.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENot a known case of DM, HTN, CVA, CAD, thyroid disorders, asthma and epilepsy.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003EPersonal history\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cu\u003EDaily routine\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient wakes up at 5 am, goes for a walk to get milk, and returns home. He then has tea with biscuits and rice for breakfast, then leaves for his work by 9 am.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHe has rice, for lunch, with curries at his workplace.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHe comes back from work at either 7 or 8 pm.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHe has rice for dinner at 9 pm and goes to sleep by 10 pm.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDiet - mixed\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAppetite - decreased since 2 month\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBowel - irregular , once 3 days and watery in consistency since 10 days , resolved now.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBladder - burning micturition since 20 days.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESleep - adequate\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAddictions - 90 ml occassionally since 35 years.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003EFamily history\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo similar complaints\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr experiences with general cellular and neural cellular pathology in a case based blended learning ecosystem's CBBLE"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cdiv\u003E30th May 2023\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EA medical student learns best with the help of experienced mentors, supportive peers and the patients that he\/she comes across.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EI am Sanjana, a medical student from India.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAs a part of my curriculum, I had the opportunity to interact with real patients during my clinical rotations and learnt many valuable lessons from them that I could not have learnt from textbooks or lectures.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHere are some of my experiences, that have pushed me to have a better clinical insight and to develop my skills.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003ECBBLE PAJR PARTICIPATORY LEARNING ACTION RESEARCH DISCLAIMER\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENOTE: THIS IS AN ONLINE E LOGBOOK TO DISCUSS OUR PATIENT'S DE-IDENTIFIED HEALTH DATA SHARED AFTER TAKING HIS\/HER GUARDIAN'S SIGNED INFORMED CONSENT. HERE WE DISCUSS OUR INDIVIDUAL PATIENT'S PROBLEMS THROUGH A SERIES OF INPUTS FROM THE AVAILABLE GLOBAL ONLINE COMMUNITY OF EXPERTS INTENDING TO SOLVE THOSE CLINICAL PROBLEMS WITH COLLECTIVE CURRENT BEST EVIDENCE-BASED INPUT\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EMy first case was a 65 year old female, accompanied by her daughter, who came with a complaint of decreased urine output since 4 days. On further questioning the patient, she said that she wasn't actually passing any urine since a day.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ETo me, her problem seemed to be a rather direct one, giving the impression of an acute kidney injury, requiring no further thought.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EBut on asking her how the symptoms had progressed and how they had occurred, she actually had a history of a surgery for which she took NSAIDS for pain control, that caused her kidney dysfunction.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EA year later, she noticed decreased urine output and on visiting various other hospitals, she was advised dialysis for which she came to KIMS.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ehttp:\/\/sanjanakulakarni140.blogspot.com\/2022\/10\/65-year-old-female-with-decreased-urine.html\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EFor someone who hasn't been able to connect the symptoms of a patient and have a deeper insight into what might be the cause of a particular disease, this came across as a lesson and will be etched into my mind whenever I see any other patient.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThus the relevant history and examination, as one may think, is never limited to the system that the patient complaints of, and that is something that I've learnt during my postings.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAnother case of a 32 year old male who came with his wife, with the complaint of not passing stools since 2 days, wherein the patient also had history of abdominal pain since many years due to alcohol consumption without taking food.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EI couldn't help but notice that his wife was very concerned about his habit of alcohol intake.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThis made me realise how one's lifestyle can not only affect them, but their family too. The patient's daily routine had little to no physical activity and he had alcohol every single day.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe patient also had abdominal distension, yellowing of the sclera and on examination he had altered liver function tests, i.e, his ALP levels and his bilirubin levels were high.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPatient also had decreased appetite.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAll these were signs of alcohol hepatitis and the patient was advised to abstain from alcohol intake.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ehttp:\/\/sanjanakulakarni140.blogspot.com\/2023\/01\/32-year-old-male-with-abdominal-pain.html\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EMy interaction with patients through clinical rounds and case taking has helped me\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-Gain practical experience and skills\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- Develop empathy and communication abilities that help build rapport with patients\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- Learn under the guidance of experienced mentors\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- Facing challenges and recognizing areas of weaknesses for further improvement to provide better quality of life for the patients.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E"},"link":[{"rel":"replies","type":"application/atom+xml","href":"https:\/\/sanjanakulakarni140.blogspot.com\/feeds\/5846772765364027874\/comments\/default","title":"Post - SHORT CASE"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: large;\"\u003EThis is an online e log book to discuss our patient de-identified health data shared after taking his \/ her \/ guardians signed informed consent. Here we discuss our individual patients problems through series of inputs from available global online community of experts with an aim to solve those patients clinical problem with collective current best evident based input.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia;
